original.closure_text: Case Closed. Closed date : 2015-09-24 08:49:30.373 Case Resolved Dear Constituent     The PWD Roadway Repair Contractor is working on your street performing patch paving.    It is an important city service for your neighborhood to provide the best permanent repairs of previous utility excavations or potholes.    The utility work previously done on your street was left with a temporary patch.    The City of Boston does not want the permanent asphalt cross section (typically 6.5" on residential street and 7.5"on main arterials) to be put back after the gravel down to the pipe has been disturbed.    There is a possibility that settlement could occur. Thats why the City waits before performing the cross section repair.  Our permanent patches hardly ever settle and that is the goal that any City or Town would want to happen regarding utility excavation work.    We do have a unit that inspects backfilling and temporary patches (The Construction Inspection Unit CIU) The CIU does stay on top of the contractors and utility companies.  Many of the temporary patches are in good condition.    However  the key is the patch is only 3".  We need the full cross section put back.    This is what you are seeing being done on your street right now.    Below is the steps taken to do the permanent repair.    The construction process is to dig out 6.5 to 7.5" inches of material and place 5 inches of dense binder hot mix asphalt in 2 lifts. The dense binder gives the patch its strength but is has large stones and is not conducive to providing a smooth ride  the contractor usually within a week comes back and places 1.5 inches of the top course. The top course is hot mix asphalt that provides the smooth ride.    I hope this explanation clarifies things for you.    If not please don't hesitate to call me.    Sincerely     Mark Cardarelli  Supervisor of Utility Coordination and Compliance  Boston Public Works Department
